author: Mark Atwood
text:
Fixed. The premise was wrong in an instructive way: removeFromCRL was implemented and correct the whole time -- pkix-revocation's own pkits_4_15_5_valid_delta_remove_from_crl passes, and 26 of 26 PKITS CRL vectors pass at that layer. The disagreement with NIST was manufactured by pkix-difftest's oracle.

build_checkers offered both a base+delta checker and a bare base checker for the same base, and check_revocation fails closed on the first revocation any checker reports. So the bare base's certificateHold always won and removeFromCRL could never take effect. A base CRL and its delta are not two opinions to weigh: the delta supersedes the base.

Two sites had to change, and the first fix alone was insufficient: a second construction site added a bare signer-discovery checker for every non-delta CRL, bypassing the guard. Signer discovery now lives inside build_checkers under the same supersession guard, because the lesson is that one rule in one place plus a second site outside it is not a guard at all.

Baseline: ground-truth disagreements 2 -> 1, and exactly one chain changed classification (4.15.5, StricterThanWild -> LooserThanWild, since pyca still carries the gap while we and OpenSSL now agree with NIST). Only PKIX-vb4o (DSA unimplemented) remains.

Regression tests in pkix-difftest/tests/pkix_path_oracle_crl.rs, both directions: 4.15.5 must pass, and 4.15.3 (revoked in base, not released by the delta) must still fail. Mutation-verified -- reinstating the bug fails the first and leaves the second passing.

Also documented the trap on CrlChecker::with_delta. The harness made this mistake naturally, so a consumer can too, and it is fail-closed and therefore easy to miss. pkix-revocation 0.5.2 for the doc change.
